clue.text: Meaty cut of Becks' fee arrangement he pocketed

indicators.note: what is pocketed is held inside, so one piece goes within the other
an arrangement of the footballer's fee reorders its letters, so the fodder is shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe: David Beckham's fee deal turns out to be a mere slab of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Becks is the nickname of the footballer David Beckham; 'arrangement' rearranges his fee into BEEFCEEKS, which 'pocketed' then wraps around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox cheeks are a slow-cooking cut of beef sold by butchers, so they are a cut of meat.

clue.text: Sing for money in coach heading for Kettering

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, taken here from Kettering

explanation.surface: A performer sings for cash aboard a coach bound for Kettering, a Northamptonshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like the coach's destination, but it takes the opening letter of Kettering.
explanation.definitionFit: Street performers who play or sing in public for coins are said to busk.

clue.text: Eat out, vomit, throwing up starter in restaurant

indicators.note: throwing something up means discarding it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to retch is to heave as if about to vomit

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, taken from restaurant

explanation.surface: A grim dining-out story: a meal at a restaurant ends with someone being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' sits in the surface as being sick, but here it means getting rid of the R that starts 'restaurant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by corroding it away, literally eating out the surface.

clue.text: Pâté ingredient taken from bird I have throttled with both hands

parts.note: a chicken is a farmyard bird

indicators.note: something throttled is gripped round the neck, so the hands go around the other piece

parts.note: left and right hands, L and R
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A grisly cook's confession: the pâté comes from a bird strangled with bare hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver of a hen is a common base for a smooth meat pâté.

clue.text: Toast might have this to encourage

definitions.meaning: a topping of fried or poached egg is often served sitting on toast
to urge someone forward or spur them on

explanation.surface: Breakfast advice that doubles as a pep talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurring someone on is to egg them on, and egg is placed on toast at breakfast.

clue.text: One can cut through a tricky situation

definitions.meaning: a blade's sharp edge is the part that slices

explanation.surface: Someone who can resolve any awkward predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade's sharpened edge slices things, and a finely balanced, risky position is described as on a knife-edge.

clue.text: Skip first course on the menu in the Groucho Club?

definitions.text: on the menu in the Groucho Club?
definitions.note: read as the bill of fare for Groucho Marx: a film he starred in

parts.note: to duck something is to dodge or skip it
soup is the usual starter of a meal

explanation.surface: A diner at the Groucho Club, a London media members' club, passes on the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Groucho Club is a Soho club for media folk, but here 'Groucho' is Groucho Marx, and 'on the menu' means one of his films.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck Soup is the 1933 Marx Brothers film comedy, so it featured Groucho in his own sort of club.

clue.text: Ruling a no.1 criminally plagiarised

parts.note: the abbreviation NO plus the numeral 1 written as the letter I

explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarised work is copied from someone else, so it lacks originality.

clue.text: Fashion accessories to draw those who sleep around

to tie a game is to draw it

explanation.surface: Accessories that attract the bed-hopping crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleep around' reads as promiscuity, but 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipper ties are the very wide neckties fashionable in the 1970s.

clue.text: Taking in fluid, I'm given PG Tips one's heated on a 22?

I am, the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone sipping a hot drink of PG Tips, a popular British tea brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is SPIT, a rod for roasting meat over a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A young piglet still on milk is traditionally roasted whole over a fire.

clue.text: See 6
Leaves battle, muscle being torn

explanation.surface: A soldier quits the fight after tearing a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is the salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb's lettuce, also called corn salad, is a small leafy salad green.

clue.text: Leaves kid drunk outside pub, getting torn off a strip

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit outside the other piece, around it
being drunk means not straight, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A child walks out of a pub drunk and gets a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the verb of the surface but is anagram fodder; 'drunk' rearranges LEAVES KID into SKEDALIVE, which 'outside' wraps round the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British idioms for being severely scolded or punished.

clue.text: Take bets on Wilder getting the chop

indicators.note: made wilder means less ordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bookmaker takes bets on whether a manager named Wilder will be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like a name (Chris Wilder, the football manager) but is the anagram signal; 'getting the chop' is the sack in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is a thick cut of beef on the bone, a kind of chop.

clue.text: One in black suit?

parts.note: one is the card valued one, in clubs, a black suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in a dark suit, a mourner or a bouncer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the card counting as one, and the 'suit' is the playing-card kind, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The single-pip card of the club suit, which is black in a pack of cards.

clue.text: 9's skin product cured a conservative Republican in a difficult situation

explanation.walkthrough: 9 is SUCKING PIG, so the definition means the cured skin of a pig.

clue.text: Pep talks given thus, when at home?

definitions.text: Pep talks given thus, when at home?

parts.words: Pep talks given thus, when at home?
parts.note: Pep Guardiola, the Catalan football coach, would speak his native tongue at home

explanation.surface: How motivational speeches are delivered by someone at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pep talks' are rousing speeches in the surface, but Pep is Guardiola, the manager of Manchester City, who is from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The language used by a man from Spain among his family is his native Iberian tongue.

clue.text: Minor celebrities seen regularly in Bel Air street

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Second-tier stars spotted cruising the roads of Bel Air, the wealthy Los Angeles district.
explanation.definitionFit: The second tier of famous people, below the top A-group, are known as such.

clue.text: Israeli leader to complain about Ruth's mother-in-law

parts.note: to moan is to complain

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

clue.text: Secure accommodation of slippery individual caught in dramatic setting

parts.note: a stage is where drama is performed

clue.text: Spies PA leaving railway lavatory

clue.text: Spirit shown by those putting English first

clue.text: Second mine that's dug by spade?

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner's second shaft dug out by spade.
explanation.definitionFit: The depth of soil turned by one spade blade is a gardener's unit.

clue.text: Club serving up Japanese seaweed

parts.note: nori is the seaweed wrapping sushi

clue.text: Fox skinned birds

parts.note: to fox someone is to bemuse or baffle them

explanation.surface: A fox strips the feathers off some birds.

clue.text: Fine sushi rolls quiet salesman sent back — it must have chips!

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

clue.text: Peck travels down piste back to front
